### The Valley of Decision
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Truth For Life
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-may-12-2024.html
Passage: Ruth 1:16
Points:
- Orpah chose the sensible path by staying in Moab, while Ruth abandoned familiar security for the unknown.
- Ruth recognized that staying with Naomi meant renouncing pagan gods to embrace the God of Israel.
- Her crossroad mirrors Christ's demanding call to forsake worldly comfort and self-reliance to follow Him.
- Walking in faith requires daily, conscious choices to risk personal convenience for God's truth and kingdom.

### Ruth: Godly Resolve
Author: John MacArthur
Site: Grace to You
URL: https://www.gty.org/blogs/B170214/ruth-godly-resolve
Passage: Ruth 1:16-17
Points:
- Naomi's urging to return home served to test whether Ruth had a genuine commitment to Israel's God.
- Ruth replied with a poetic, unwavering declaration of lifelong allegiance to Naomi and her community.
- Despite growing up in a pagan culture, Ruth showed an extraordinarily deep and mature personal faith.
- Ruth's resolve to leave everything behind placed her securely beneath the providential wings of God.

### Turning Your Back
Author: Joan Walker Hahn
Site: Encouragement Café
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/turning-your-back-encouragement-caf-april-18-2019.html
Passage: Ruth 1:16
Points:
- Ruth could only participate in eventual redemption by leaving behind her homeland, past idols, and familiarity.
- Christians must evaluate whether their daily lives are truly distinct from the patterns of the surrounding world.
- True devotion demands surrendering personal idols and prioritizing Christ even above good earthly pursuits.
- Following the Lord resembles a bride's exclusive love, kept alive through continuous awareness of His presence.

### Ruth and Naomi
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/ruth-and-naomi
Passage: Ruth 1:16-17
Points:
- Naomi expected her widowed daughters-in-law to seek earthly security among the regional gods of Moab.
- In contrast to Orpah, Ruth completely abandoned Moabite deities to serve the one true God of Israel.
- Amid the pervasive spiritual darkness of the period of the judges, Ruth's commitment stood out as exemplary.
- Ruth's sudden faith and resolve demonstrated God's supernatural grace awakening and regenerating a heart.
